content.title: Can anyone tell me about me about the dress code? — Ruth's Chris Steak House
content.text: Ask the Yelp Forum About Ruth's Chris Steak HouseRuth's Chris Steak House3.8(1.1k reviews)Steakhouses, Seafood, Wine BarsRuth's Chris Steak House PhotosFood was on pointFilet with blue cheeseCreme BruleeCan anyone tell me about me about the dress code?Asked by Brianna H.9 years ago13 AnswersSort byPopularTee E.116422I would describe the main dining room as dressy. I haven't heard they mandate suit jackets but no sneakers or sports wear. The bar are is a bit more casual. At Ruth's Chris Chicago I've seen men turned away for jeans that were too casual and asked to remove hats.9 years agoHelpful 10 Not HelpfulTri A.01084Dress casual but no shorts and flip flops. It's on the site of ruth chris9 years agoHelpful 4 Not HelpfulJames L.1276Very casual, no shorts or flip flops. When we were there we just came from the theater and people were nicely dressed9 years agoHelpful 3 Not HelpfulTerry W.13170As with most steak houses, many of Ruth's Chris' patrons are people on business accounts, therefore many, especially in the afternoon, are wearing business attire. However, this restaurant also attracts many tourists, so the attire is casual. Anyway, I believe any fashion, as long as not torn t-shirts, torn jeans, etc. is fine. Whatever makes you comfortable while eating great steaks.9 years agoHelpful 3 Not HelpfulGarynn N.241140150I wouldn't say there's a "dress code" per se, but you might feel out of place while dining if you're in jeans and a t-shirt. I'd say casual is fine for a woman if she does jeans with heels, but if a dress is an option I'd go with a dress. During the week it's mostly business and business casual in there.9 years agoHelpful 5 Not HelpfulMarios C.133117Business casual. They have a posted dress code that I totally agree with but unfortunately they do not abide by it because of the tourists. Nothing worse than arriving properly well dressed for a premium priced $$$ steak dinner in a classy setting and you end up eating next to a bunch of tourists in sweatpants, tacky t-shirts and flip flops. This is New York, we dress up when we go out to eat, tank tops and flip flops are for Applebee's.7 years agoHelpful 1 Not HelpfulDavid M.0135We dined in the midtown location Friday night. It was a 'date night' for me and my wife, and after reading the dress code I wore nice pants, dress shirt and sports coat. Other people were dressed similarly. However there were quite a few folks, mostly tourists, wearing hoodies, sweatpants, t shirts, baseball caps and other streetwear which made the whole place feel very casual and downmarket. If Ruth Chris has a dress code they should stick by it.7 years agoHelpful 1 Not HelpfulA C.0951431It's definitely business casual. There is a sign at the hostess stand that states this policy. I was wearing black tights and sneakers and they would have turned me away except that since I was there for an event in the back room where I wouldn't be seen, they let me in.9 years agoHelpful 1 Not HelpfulCarlo J.010Believe it or not This location turned down a party of 12 for a birthday celebration because one out of the party a 10 year old boy who is 4 '7 and 85 pounds had on grey sweat pants. children are subjected to dress code here as well and their manager is very rude as well. I argued how could a dress code be enforce on children ? The manager said its just the policy now and do not seem not to care about if the child was of age or not. Very disappointing never will dine there again 9 years agoHelpful 10 Not HelpfulKim W.24915Just dress casual nice slacks shoes blouse it's fine dining..9 years agoHelpful 2 Not Helpful121 of 2Help out
